summary.headline: GRP Q2 FY27 PAT more than tripled to INR64 million on 30% revenue growth, with EBITDA margin steady at about 11% despite a 5-point gross margin fall.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose 30% YoY to INR1,727 million in Q2 FY27, and EBITDA grew 60% to INR182 million at a 10.5% margin (up 199 bps). Gross margin fell to 46% from 51% on raw material inflation, offset by volume growth, manpower productivity, energy savings and newer businesses. H1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 10.8% versus 8.6%, and working capital days fell to 84 from 95. Management said Pyrova Energy turned operationally profitable in Q2 and targets a mid-teens EBITDA margin for the platform once rCB and pyrolysis expansion are complete.

segments.name: Rubber recycling (standalone reclaim rubber)
segments.commentary: Standalone segment revenue grew 30% in H1 FY27 and reclaim rubber volumes grew 8%. About one-third of reclaim rubber sales volume now comes from the new downstream technology, which management says saves about 2-3% of overall cost.

segments.name: Pyrova Energy (pyrolysis / rCB / EPR)
segments.commentary: Cumulative investment was INR1,140 million at end-September, including INR110 million CWIP. First EPR income was booked in Q2 FY27 after registration, and management said Q2 was the first quarter of positive contribution. Pyrolysis capacity is to rise from 15,000 to 45,000 tons per annum by March 2027.

segments.name: Plastics recycling
segments.commentary: Consolidated plastics revenue grew 38% YoY in H1 FY27 and EBITDA margin improved by 11 percentage points. Management guided about 20% growth this year at a stable 12-15% EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: Platform EBITDA margin target of mid-teens once rCB and pyrolysis scale-up are complete; management said it is on track as things stand.
Pyrolysis expansion from 15,000 to 45,000 tons: equipment commissioning around end-March to early April 2027, with about 30-60 days to stabilise, so full impact from Q2 FY28.
Plastics: about 20% growth this fiscal year at a 12-15% EBITDA margin; management aspires to high double-digit growth thereafter.
Renewables expected to cross the 50% target share of standalone power after the Gujarat Solar project commissioning (48% in FY26).
Solapur facility (rCB plus pyrolysis) total investment about INR140 crore for about 45,000 tons pyrolysis and about 15,000 tons rCB, targeting about 2x asset turns.
capex_capacity: Total H1 FY27 capex was INR246 million.
Pyrova cumulative capex about INR114 crore at 30 September 2026, including INR11 crore CWIP (call also cites INR1,140 million and INR110 million CWIP, a units discrepancy in the transcript).
rCB facility at Solapur expected to be commissioned by end of Q3 FY27 (end of the quarter in which the call was held); capacity about 15,000 tons.
ECB of up to EUR12 million from PROPARCO; EUR7.5 million drawn, unchanged since 31 March 2026.
Funding from internal accruals and long-term debt.
demand_pricing: Management said export volumes recovered after the US tariff reset, while India was the stronger market; reclaimed rubber consumption in India rose 5% YoY in the June quarter.

Raw material costs rose sharply on crude (from mid-USD60 to about USD100/bbl), elevated natural rubber prices, and tighter waste tire imports on freight costs, pushing domestic end-of-life tire prices up.
Gross margin pressure also came from Pyrova's conversion-linked lower margin and additional export freight costs.
Pyrolysis oil realisations track crude and furnace oil; management warned that current elevated levels may not persist and should not be taken as the run rate.
Management declined to give an EBITDA per ton for rCB or comment on competitors' rCB quality, as the commercial rCB plant is not yet operational (only a pilot plant exists).

qa_highlights.question: What is the procurement strategy for pyrolysis, given imports are prohibited, and what is the regulatory outlook and cause of raw material price rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pyrolysis relies only on domestic waste and EPR credits are based on domestic sourcing. Imported material is used for reclaim rubber under Advance Licences. Raw material price pressure is partly geopolitical and partly from tighter imports, and some tires may end up in unorganised pyrolysis. Representations to allow pyrolysis imports exist but management could not comment on their status.

qa_highlights.question: Quality improvement steps for rCB versus virgin carbon black, and EBITDA target per ton for rCB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified the commercial rCB plant is not operational and only a pilot plant exists. It declined to give rCB-specific EBITDA, saying it reports platform-level numbers, and targets a mid-teens EBITDA margin for the whole platform versus 11% now.

qa_highlights.question: How do gross margins fall 529 bps yet EBITDA margin rise about 200 bps; what share and economics do new reclaim technologies have?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin fell on Pyrova's lower conversion-linked margin and export freight. EBITDA was supported by efficiencies, mainly energy. About one-third of reclaim rubber volume now uses the new downstream technology, saving about 2-3% of overall cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much of plastics turnaround is mix and realisation versus efficiency; sustainable margin and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both product and customer mix shift toward value-added applications and efficiency gains. Guidance is about 20% growth this year at 12-15% EBITDA margin, with a long-term view that plastics could be as large as or larger than tire recycling, pursued cautiously.

qa_highlights.question: Underlying profitability excluding EPR, and sustainability of EPR income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPR is now embedded in operations and partly in industry pricing, and that India's EPR regime is more stable than most sectors. It acknowledged some credit leakage to unorganised recyclers, which government audits are addressing. No ex-EPR figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Pyrolysis ramp-up timeline, utilisation, revenue, EBITDA and ROCE potential; Pyrova investment and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: The first reactor line took 4-5 months to stabilise, but the next two lines should take 30-60 days. Utilisation needs to be close to 95%. Management expects about 2x asset turns and mid-teens EBITDA margin. Q2 was the first positive-contribution quarter, but profit is not yet at healthy levels; INR114 crore reflects shared infrastructure and rCB, so it is not representative of full investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the effective tax rate so volatile (around 55% last year)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 included a short provision for past taxes of about INR1.7 crore, now regularised, and Q2 is normalised. Earlier years were affected by a one-time transfer from the old to the new tax regime.

risks_watch: Pyrova margins depend on crude and furnace oil prices, which management said may normalise and soften realisations.
Domestic end-of-life tire feedstock availability and pricing, given tighter imports and possible unorganised-sector pyrolysis use; pyrolysis imports remain prohibited.
rCB commissioning (Solapur) and market qualification: the commercial plant is not yet operational and product quality versus competitors is unproven.
Pyrolysis expansion to 45,000 tons on schedule (end-March/early April 2027), and reaching 95% utilisation.
EPR income quality: credit leakage to informal recyclers and possible regulatory changes; Q2 EPR income was INR67 million, a significant share of total income.
Working capital: rising domestic receivables (pricing, credit) and debt-to-equity up to 1.13x.
Export freight and tariff exposure, and gross margin at 46% versus 51% a year ago.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the operating turnaround and EBITDA stability, but cautious on energy-linked Pyrova earnings and the geopolitical outlook. Management was evasive on rCB specifics and on pyrolysis import rules, and it repeatedly declined to give a segment EBITDA figure.
key_quotes: For 2 consecutive quarters, we have held EBITDA margins at around 11%, and we have done this while gross margins fell by 5 percentage points because of raw material inflation.
Our commercial plant for manufacturing rCB is not operational at all. Currently, we have a pilot plant, and that is only to see the market.
I think Q2 was the first quarter where the business was, what you call, positive contribution.

These prices may, may not last. And if energy markets do normalize, the realizations will soften and investors, therefore, should not take the current level as the necessary run rate for Pyrova as a business.
I can't comment right now because our plant itself is not operational.
